holidays.name: Draw a Bird Day
holidays.description: Grab a pencil, crayon, or finger-paint and draw a bird. It could be a majestic eagle or a lopsided pigeon. Skill doesn't matter. The point is to have fun and share your feathered masterpiece with others.
holidays.origin: The day started in 1947. A young girl asked a hospital patient to cheer up her father by drawing a bird. The day was first marked on what would have been her birthday, and it has grown into a worldwide tradition of sharing bird drawings to spread happiness.
holidays.funFact: The holiday has no skill requirement. It's all about sharing happiness, and people are invited to send in their bird drawings to be shared.

holidays.name: National Empanada Day
holidays.description: A day for savoring the golden, flaky, stuffed pastry that is beloved across Latin America and Spain. Fillings range from spiced beef and cheese to chicken, corn, and sweet fruit. Bake them or fry them, and eat them by hand.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance, and its origin is unclear. The empanada itself goes back centuries to Spain and Portugal. The name comes from the Spanish word for wrapping something in bread.
holidays.funFact: The word empanada comes from the Spanish verb empanar, which means to wrap or coat in bread.

holidays.name: National Zoo Lovers Day
holidays.description: A day to visit your local zoo and cheer on the penguins, lions, and sloths. It's a good excuse to stand in front of the otter exhibit for far too long.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It falls in spring, when many zoos see their animals become more active and visitors return.
holidays.funFact: Many modern zoos take part in species survival programs, which coordinate breeding of endangered animals across institutions worldwide.
